coverage: overnight / since evening (~12–18h; last evening ~19:00 Berlin)
headline: OpenAI ships GPT-6 Sol and Luna at half prior API prices; ShinyHunters claims FBI employee data theft; SF sues Truth Social over paid early access to Trump posts.

stories.title: OpenAI expands GPT-6 with Sol and Luna — 50% cheaper API tiers
facts: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol (coding/agentic) and GPT-6 Luna (fast, high-volume tasks), building on GPT-6 Astra with lower cost and higher usage limits.
API list prices cut 50% vs GPT-5.6 promos: Sol $2/$10 and Luna $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens; company cites caching and inference gains.
OpenAI says Sol makes ~half as many factual mistakes as its predecessor on an internal real-conversation eval, approaching Astra-level reliability at lower cost.
Available now as gpt-6-sol / gpt-6-luna in the API and in ChatGPT Work + Codex for Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise/Edu; Free/Go get Luna in the desktop app; Chat rollout gradual.
TechCrunch notes Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 landed ~90 minutes earlier — the overnight HN thread (~1.4k points) treats the pair as a same-evening model race.
stories.whyItMatters: After evening’s Opus 5.5 lead, OpenAI’s cheaper GPT-6 mid-tier models are the clear overnight follow-through for builders watching cost-per-task, not just frontier benchmarks.

stories.title: ShinyHunters claim FBI employee/applicant data dump; bureau investigating FBIjobs.gov
facts: ShinyHunters told 404 Media it breached FBI-related systems and holds data “on all FBI employees and applicants,” sharing a ~5,000-record sample (names, addresses, phones, DOBs; some spouse fields).
Group claims an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day path into AWS GovCloud and 2–3 TB exfiltrated; apply.fbijobs.gov was defaced and the Special Agent Applicant Portal showed unavailable.
FBI (via CNN): aware of unauthorized-activity claims affecting FBIjobs.gov and investigating — has not publicly verified full dump scope or authenticity.
404 Media says some sample fields matched real people; CNN reports the FBI is investigating unauthorized activity on FBIjobs.gov without confirming the dump’s full scope.
stories.whyItMatters: If even partially real, a personnel PII breach at this scale is a counterintelligence and agent-safety problem — not just another website defacement.

stories.title: San Francisco sues Truth Social parent over paid early access to Trump posts
facts: SF City Attorney David Chiu sued Trump Media (Sep 22) alleging Truth API sells firms a ~50 ms head start on market-moving Truth posts for up to $100k/month.
Complaint says the feed covers the platform’s ten most influential accounts — including Trump and other White House officials — and that Trump remains the largest shareholder (~41% via trust).
City cites examples after Truth API went live Aug 1 (e.g., Iran-strike call-off moving oil; tariff-free ground-beef post moving cattle futures) and seeks an injunction plus UCL civil penalties.
heise flagged the case overnight for German readers as “Echtzeitzugriff” on Trump posts.
stories.whyItMatters: Turns a social product into an alleged pay-to-play wire for presidential market information — and puts a major US city on the plaintiff side.

stories.title: Alibaba unveils Zhenwu V900 chip and multi-trillion-parameter model plans
facts: At its Hangzhou Apsara conference (Tue), Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu called the new Zhenwu V900 “the most powerful AI chip in China today,” claiming ~3× the prior Zhenwu M890.
Company said it plans to train a next model at 5–10 trillion parameters; current flagship Qwen3.8-Max is listed at 2.4 trillion.
Alibaba also guided to >20 GW of cloud/AI compute capacity by 2032, citing exponential demand and supply-chain constraints on how fast it can scale.
AP notes the unveil comes days ahead of Xi’s Washington visit with Trump, where AI competition is expected on the agenda.
stories.whyItMatters: Another mainland self-reliance signal on chips and scale — timed for the US–China leadership meeting window.

stories.title: Bloomberg: Pentagon probe ties Minab school strike to stale intel + AI overreliance
facts: Pentagon review officials told Bloomberg that stale intel, outdated imagery, rushed timelines, thin civilian-harm staffing, and overreliance on Palantir’s Maven contributed to the Feb 28 Minab school strike.

Reporting says two Tomahawks hit Shajarah Tayyebeh Elementary; death tolls cited around 123 children / 150+ total (UN-backed fact-finding has separately discussed war-crimes findings on February Iran strikes).

Some Centcom personnel reportedly expected Maven to flag stale or contradictory data; Palantir told Bloomberg it is “not responsible for the underlying data” and denies evidence its software was at fault.
Story resurged overnight on HN (~557 points) even though the Bloomberg investigation landed earlier in the week — still absent from yesterday’s evening brief.
stories.whyItMatters: Puts a concrete kill-chain failure next to the same AI-targeting stack the Pentagon has been racing to standardize.

image.alt: When you see this logo on any artwork, whether painting, poetry, or prose, you know that it was made by a human just like you The Brainmade mark can be attached to any work made mostly by you or your friends, not generative tools like GPT. It’s not anti-AI, it is a positive mark that celebrates human creation. It’s not AI = bad, it’s human = good. There’s something transcendent and magical in knowing a human made the artwork I’m consuming, knowing they tried hard is part of the experience. It doesn’t have to be 100% human made (what would that even MEAN these days?), perhaps 90% human made. I don’t hate AIs, I love humans!
